references.text: Refers to 'a covenant of salt' (בְּרִית מֶלַח) that God gave to Aaron and his sons, emphasizing the significance of salt in covenant relationships.
Describes God's kingdom given to David through 'a covenant of salt', illustrating salt's symbolic meaning for eternal and unbreakable covenants.
In Ezekiel's temple vision, priests are to sprinkle salt on the burnt offering, confirming the continued practice of using salt in sacrifices.
Jesus speaks that 'every sacrifice must be seasoned with salt' and encourages disciples to have salt within themselves, referencing the sacrificial laws.
Paul urges that speech should be 'seasoned with salt', drawing on salt's purifying and preserving symbolism from the context of sacrifices.
Complementary instructions for the composition of the grain offering: oil/frankincense (v.1) and salt as a covenant symbol (v.13).
